propositions: Two concurrent reconciler passes can reach the same-target save() on .bridge_state sidecars due to lease-steal window and missing abort_check guard before persistence-phase write, causing FileNotFoundError and silent data loss when both writers share a deterministic temp name

PeerConfirmationStore.save() and ImpossibleLinkStore.save() use shared f"{self.path}.tmp" deterministic temp followed by os.replace, violating the package's standardized unique-per-writer tempfile.mkstemp pattern already applied to five other atomic-write sites

The fail-open error-swallow behavior (OSError caught and logged) masks the collision: the second os.replace raises FileNotFoundError, the exception is swallowed, and the losing writer's _dirty flag never clears, leaving stale temp residue

Fix requires replacing deterministic shared temp with unique-per-writer tempfile.mkstemp, atomic os.replace onto shared final path, and cleanup-only (unlink own temp) on failure, preserving last-write-wins and fail-open contract

Regression RED→GREEN test at test_bridge_state_atomic_write_concurrency.py proves both stores persist _dirty state cleared under concurrent same-target writers with unique temps, and mutation-revert to shared temp returns RED
